label: ex:topological-mass-su2
title: Topological mass decomposition for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$
html:
Example. Topological mass decomposition for \mathrm{SU}(2)

Continuing the descent eigenspaces for SU(2), we verify the topological mass theorem for G = \mathrm{SU}(2).

The decomposition. By the topological mass theorem, the mass of a cycle \varrho decomposes according to the eigenspace splitting:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) =  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho),

where \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the descended (persistent) contribution and \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the transient contribution.

Descended mass. The descended trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}} factors through the projection \hat{\tau} onto \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \cong \mathfrak{su}(2). For the Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1, the descended mass of the fundamental cycle evaluates to:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} =  \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) =  2,

which is the Euler characteristic of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2. This provides the topologically protected part. It remains invariant under continuous deformations of the cycle and the metric.

Transient mass. The transient trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}} captures fluctuations in the cotangent directions \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} \cong \Omega^1(\mathbb{CP}^1) \oplus \mathbb{C}. For a cycle \varrho that is \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant, \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) = 0 since the transient eigenspace has non-zero \mathrm{U}(1)-weight. Non-equivariant deformations of \varrho contribute a non-zero \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} that measures the departure from the symmetric configuration.

Total mass. For the fundamental cycle of the Hopf fibration, m = 2 + 0 = 2, recovering the Euler characteristic. For a deformed cycle, m = 2 + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}, with the correction depending on the L^2-norm of the cotangent component.
